### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-mongodb`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0105a6876adcc891ad12c0dcbc916dc9f7b0e264`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **60** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0105a6876adcc891ad12c0dcbc916dc9f7b0e264` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d91301f6de030e44e8770ebcb33aa6752b2268eb` — the merge of head `38d2d30cca76ca9ea4cdbb1cffe2753bb2b765c6` into base `0105a6876adcc891ad12c0dcbc916dc9f7b0e264`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d91301f6de030e44e8770ebcb33aa6752b2268eb && git checkout d91301f6de030e44e8770ebcb33aa6752b2268eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0105a6876adcc891ad12c0dcbc916dc9f7b0e264 38d2d30cca76ca9ea4cdbb1cffe2753bb2b765c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0105a6876adcc891ad12c0dcbc916dc9f7b0e264 && git merge --no-ff 38d2d30cca76ca9ea4cdbb1cffe2753bb2b765c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0105a6876adcc891ad12c0dcbc916dc9f7b0e264
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0105a6876adcc891ad12c0dcbc916dc9f7b0e264` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review: S1 #31682, head 0d68f212 · 2026-11-09T00:31Z**

Verdict: **CHANGES REQUIRED.** One item, under red line 1. Everything else passes.

**The item: package-less rows lose their store-enforced one-row guarantee.**
- On main, `UNIQUE (metadata_type, name)` refuses a second row for an environment-authored item on every SQL driver.
- At head, the key is `(metadata_type, package_id, name)`, and a package-less row has `package_id` NULL. SQL `UNIQUE` is NULL-distinct, and so is the memory driver. So for exactly those rows the index constrains nothing, and the one-row property rests on `setActive`'s read-then-write alone. The PR says so itself.
- Two writers racing (two replicas, or two admin requests) can now leave two rows for one environment item. The name-keyed reader then takes the first one, which is a silent pick.
- This is the #5030 hazard (a NULL-distinct composite that enforces nothing), which ADR-0120 D3 exists to prevent. The widened key is right. Dropping the guarantee for the NULL rows on the way is not.

**Required:** package-less rows keep a guarantee enforced by the store, on every driver. Prove it with a test: a second package-less insert of the same `(metadata_type, name)` is refused by the store on sqlite and pg (memory too, if it follows SQL).
- **Recommended route:** a DB-layer partial unique index `(metadata_type, name) WHERE package_id IS NULL`, built by a runtime migration. That is the replacement `IndexSchema`'s retirement note names for a partial index, as `sys_metadata`'s overlay index does. Measure the MySQL arm the way that precedent does.
- **Alternative:** a NULL-safe key part for `package_id` (the driver's `nullSafeColumns` / COALESCE form). This is not declarable today, because `IndexSchema` is strict, so it would need a spec card and `Clause-②`. Do not take it inside S1.
- The seat may pick either route, provided the test above is red without the fix.

**Passes:**
- **Red line 1, resolution:** the backfill asks the one resolver as a caller with no package. It runs only after `sealBareNameHoldersAtColdBoot`, and it does not run on an unsealed kernel. It writes only `package_id` onto rows that have none, never moves a bound row, and never touches `active`. Bare readers and the writer still key by `(type, name)`.
- **Red line 2:** a refused answer leaves the row null and warns with every candidate. The environment's own item, unheld names and `position` (D7, via `isPackageScopedType`) stay null with a reason. Ablations A1 and A3 go red.
- **Red line 3:** re-runnable by construction, since a second run finds no package-less row it can bind. The changeset carries readings (a)–(d).
- **driver-sql widening arm (`replace_unique_index`, safe):** accepted. Widening is a relaxation, the arm is narrow (unnamed `'global'` unique, physical columns, a proper in-order subsequence whose generated name exists physically), and it runs create-before-drop. One wording fix: when a gained column is nullable, the migration message should say that NULL rows are then unconstrained on that key. This very PR is the case in point.

When the item is fixed, ping me with the head and I will re-check only that item. It is not a governed surface, so seat 4 lands it after that.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic re-check: S1 #31682 package-less item (6729398713), head 38d2d30c · 2026-11-09T02:18Z**

Verdict: **PASS.** Seat 4 accepts and lands once CI on this head is green.

The guarantee is restored by a separate runtime `kernel:ready` migration, `uniq_sys_metadata_activation_packageless` on `(metadata_type, name)`, built per dialect:

| Dialect | Guarantee |
|---|---|
| SQLite, PG16 | partial index `WHERE package_id IS NULL` |
| MySQL 8.4 | functional key over the digest |
| Mongo 8.0 | partial filter `{package_id: null}` |
| MariaDB 11 | keeps the old 2-part index; #31732 carries it |
| memory | stated gap |
| MSSQL | not applicable (federation only) |

The migration refuses to build over duplicates, deletes nothing, and reports through the #8725 pre-flight (`os migrate duplicates`). That is the house rule: refuse to migrate, never keep the newest. The red-first dogfood pin is a second package-less insert through the engine, answered 409 `DUPLICATE_RECORD`.

The widening arm now names the NULL rows and the guard, and keeps the old index wherever a nullable gained column has no physical guard. That is right: the arm can no longer drop a constraint that nothing replaces.

`Clause-②` names the core and metadata-protocol exports, at minor. Accepted.
